name: @finchtoys/mcp-client
description: Connect Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers into Finch.

finch.name: MCP Client
finch.description: Connect to Model Context Protocol servers, expose their tools to the Finch, and provide an mcp.client capability for other extensions.
finch.systemPrompt: Use MCP with action=list/add/edit/remove/connect/disconnect to manage configured MCP services. For an OAuth-enabled HTTP MCP service, action=connect runs OAuth discovery, Dynamic Client Registration, and PKCE; do not check status first when the user asks to authorize. Never ask users to paste secrets in chat, because add/edit opens a secure form for secret values. For HTTP add/edit, set authMethod to none, oauth, bearer, basic, or apiKey; for API keys also pass apiKeyPlacement and apiKeyName, and use headerNames for extra business headers. Pass only non-secret metadata — the secure form collects passwords, tokens, API keys, and header values, then add/edit waits for a successful connection. Protocol headers (MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, Mcp-Param-*) are generated automatically by the client per request — never configure them as fixed custom headers, because Mcp-Name must match the request body's params.name/params.uri; a HeaderMismatch/-32020 or missing-Mcp-Name error points to client/transport protocol issues (negotiated version, SDK version, transport wrapper), not a missing custom header. To use actual MCP server tools, when the target server name is known first call Finch ToolSearch with source:"mcp:<server>"; fall back to source:"mcp" only if that precise search finds no usable tool, because mcp__<server>__<tool> names are never pre-loaded and will fail if called directly. ToolSearch connects the selected servers, discovers their tools, and injects mcp__<server>__<tool> functions into the current run. Authorization can be granted per-tool (mcp__filesystem__read_file) or with a wildcard (mcp__filesystem__*).
